item.title: Americans Are Rethinking Holiday Travel as Spending Concerns Rise
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
American holiday travel plans are showing signs of a slowdown, according to the latest Longwoods International tracking study, with more travelers expecting to cut back on both trips and spending in 2026. The October survey found that 31% of American travelers plan to travel less this holiday season than they did last year, an increase of eight percentage points from 2025 and 13 points from 2024. Meanwhile, 35% expect to spend less on holiday travel, up 11 points from the previous year, while only 16% anticipate traveling more and 22% expect to increase their spending. The broader outlook is also softening: the share of Americans with travel plans for the next six months has declined from 93% a year ago to 86%. Inflation and gasoline prices remain significant considerations, cited by 35% of respondents as major influences on their travel decisions. The survey, conducted October 6–9 among 1,000 U.S. adults, suggests that economic pressures are increasingly shaping how Americans approach the holiday travel season, although changes in fuel prices, airfares and consumer confidence could still influence demand.

The Curated Take

The findings point to a holiday season in which travel decisions may be less about abandoning travel altogether and more about reassessing its cost and value. For the luxury travel industry, that distinction matters. Travelers who remain committed to meaningful experiences may become more selective about where they go, how long they stay and what makes a journey worth the investment. Destinations and hospitality brands will need to communicate value beyond the rate itself, emphasizing distinctive experiences, thoughtful service and the reasons a trip deserves a place in the holiday budget. The coming months will reveal whether this early softness becomes a broader pullback or a more deliberate approach to travel spending.

item.title: W Maldives Brings Olympic Gold to the Indian Ocean with an Exclusive Guest Experience
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
W Maldives is adding an unexpected sporting dimension to its private-island experience this December, welcoming Taiwanese badminton champion Wang Chi-Lin for a three-day guest appearance from December 1 to 3, 2026. A two-time Olympic gold medalist who claimed consecutive men’s doubles titles at the Tokyo 2020 and Paris 2024 Games, Wang will lead a complimentary one-hour badminton coaching session for resort guests. The collaboration also extends to Marriott Bonvoy Moments, where members can bid on a more immersive experience combining private coaching with a four-night stay in an overwater villa, a sunset escape to the resort’s private island of Gaathafushi, spa treatments and guided snorkeling. Set in the North Ari Atoll, W Maldives brings together vibrant marine life, distinctive dining, wellness and the freedom of a secluded Indian Ocean setting.

The Curated Take

Luxury travel increasingly finds its distinction in experiences that cannot simply be replicated at another resort. An opportunity to learn from an Olympic champion brings a personal and memorable dimension to an island stay, while the combination of sport, marine exploration and private-island moments gives the experience a character beyond the familiar rhythms of a Maldives escape. It is an appealing example of how a resort can create meaningful connections around a guest’s interests, even in a setting already defined by extraordinary natural beauty.

item.title: This Gulf Coast Destination Is Looking Ahead to a New Era for Pensacola Tourism
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Pensacola, Florida, is preparing for its next chapter in destination development with the appointment of Tony Lyle as President and CEO of Visit Pensacola, effective October 26, 2026. Bringing more than 25 years of tourism and destination marketing experience, including his recent leadership of Visit Galveston in Texas, Lyle will guide the organization’s efforts to strengthen Pensacola’s position as a Gulf Coast travel destination. His background spans coastal tourism, international travel trade, leisure and group travel, sports tourism and destination brand development, with a focus on building partnerships and encouraging visitation beyond traditional peak travel periods. The Pensacola Bay Area offers a distinctive combination of more than 465 years of history, nearly 40 miles of sugar-white beaches and emerald Gulf waters, encompassing Pensacola, Pensacola Beach and Perdido Key. From its historic character as America’s First Settlement to its coastal appeal and evolving hospitality scene, the region brings together cultural discovery and relaxed beach escapes. Lyle’s appointment signals an opportunity to build on that identity while strengthening the partnerships and experiences that support tourism throughout Northwest Florida.

The Curated Take

A destination’s appeal is shaped by more than its beaches, hotels and attractions. The vision and partnerships behind its tourism industry also influence how a place evolves and what visitors discover when they arrive. Pensacola has a compelling foundation in its blend of Gulf Coast scenery and deep historical roots. As the destination looks toward its next chapter, the opportunity lies in bringing those elements together in ways that encourage travelers to explore beyond the shoreline and discover the broader character of the Pensacola Bay Area.

item.title: When the Sun Disappears, New Zealand Takes Center Stage
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
On July 22, 2028, a total solar eclipse will offer travelers a rare reason to explore New Zealand, and Smithsonian Journeys is building an expert-led journey around the celestial event. Scheduled for July 13–24, 2028, the 12-day experience will cross both the North and South Islands, connecting Auckland, Rotorua, Queenstown and the Southern Alps with an exclusive eclipse viewing celebration at a Gibbston Valley vineyard in Central Otago wine country. Astronomy experts will accompany the journey, offering lectures and discussions that bring the science of the eclipse into conversation with New Zealand’s natural and cultural heritage. The announcement also expands Smithsonian Journeys’ collection of eclipse-focused travel, with additional 2028 departures in Australia and journeys planned for the 2027 total solar eclipse in Spain, Morocco, Egypt and along the Iberian Peninsula. For travelers drawn to rare natural phenomena, the experience offers an opportunity to pair a remarkable moment in the night sky with a deeper exploration of a destination.

The Curated Take

Celestial events have a way of giving a journey a sense of occasion, but the most rewarding eclipse trips are about more than securing a place beneath the path of totality. The appeal of this New Zealand itinerary lies in the combination of expert interpretation, regional discovery and the setting itself. Central Otago’s vineyard landscapes provide a distinctive backdrop for the viewing, while the wider journey offers an introduction to two islands with very different natural and cultural character. With the 2027 and 2028 eclipses inspiring a growing range of expert-led journeys, astronomy is becoming an intriguing lens through which to experience the world.

item.title: The Unexpected Holiday Escape Just Outside Seattle
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Just minutes from Seattle-Tacoma International Airport, Seattle Southside is offering travelers and local visitors a variety of ways to make the holiday season part of the journey. From independent shops and locally made gifts to international markets and global dining, the region brings together experiences that extend well beyond an airport overnight. Visitors can browse specialty retailers, discover wildlife conservation gifts supporting Pacific Northwest marine rescue efforts, tour a chocolate factory or explore the area’s multicultural food scene. The destination is also highlighting its Stay, Play & Fly approach, encouraging travelers to turn an early departure, overnight connection or extended layover into a mini getaway with nearby hotels, attractions and waterfront experiences. Seasonal highlights include Thanksgiving dining, wreathmaking workshops, Burien’s Holiday Cookie Crawl, the Argosy Christmas Ship Festival at Des Moines Marina and the Rainier Symphony’s holiday concert. New additions to the area include Molly Tea, West African restaurant Taste of Jollof and an expanded Interim Computer Museum, adding further reasons to explore Seattle Southside during the festive season.

The Curated Take

Seattle Southside makes a compelling case for looking beyond the airport when traveling through the Seattle region. Its appeal lies in the combination of convenience and cultural variety: independent businesses, international food traditions, waterfront experiences and seasonal events create opportunities to turn otherwise overlooked travel time into something memorable. The emphasis on shopping small and discovering locally rooted businesses also gives the holiday experience a more personal dimension. For travelers passing through SEA, a little extra time here can offer a welcome introduction to the flavors and character of the Pacific Northwest.

item.title: The Great Migration Is a Year-Round Story, Not Just a Spectacle at the River
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
The Great Migration is often associated with one iconic safari moment: thousands of wildebeest gathering along the Mara River before attempting a crossing. But the spectacle represents only one chapter in a much larger ecological story. Lemala Camps & Lodges is bringing that broader perspective into focus with Migration 365, a new initiative designed to help travelers understand the annual rhythms of the Serengeti and the forces that shape the herds’ movements. Through its guiding teams, the campaign explores how rainfall, grazing conditions, calving seasons, predator behavior and changing landscapes influence wildlife throughout the year. The experience varies by season and location, from the southern Serengeti’s calving grounds at Lemala Ndutu Tented Camp between December and March, to the transitional months around Lemala Ewanjan, and the northern Serengeti’s migration activity near Lemala Mara Tented Camp and Lemala Kuria Hills Lodge from July through October. Lemala Nanyukie Lodge offers a year-round perspective on the region’s resident wildlife and wider ecosystem. Rather than promising a particular sighting, Migration 365 puts the emphasis on expert interpretation, helping guests understand not only what they are seeing, but why it is happening.

The Curated Take

A safari does not have to revolve around a single bucket-list encounter to be extraordinary. The Great Migration is a living ecological process, and its quieter chapters can reveal just as much about the Serengeti as the dramatic river crossings that dominate wildlife photography. Lemala’s emphasis on migration literacy gives the safari experience another dimension, turning expert guiding into an opportunity to understand the relationships between wildlife, weather and landscape. It also invites travelers to look beyond the traditional peak season, where different stages of the annual cycle offer their own distinctive encounters. For those seeking a more informed and immersive African safari, the story of the Great Migration is far richer than any one moment.

item.title: Not Every Moment Needs an Itinerary
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
In a world of increasingly packed itineraries, Aahaasa Collection is inviting travelers to experience Sri Lanka at a more deliberate pace. The boutique hospitality brand has introduced three multi-property journeys for 2026–2027, connecting its coastal, tea-country and mountain retreats through experiences shaped by nature, local culture and traditional wellness. At Aavya Cove Villas, the Indian Ocean sets the rhythm for days spent exploring mangroves, meeting local fishermen or simply enjoying the beach. At Aadya Tea Bungalows, guests can discover the traditions of a working tea estate, walk through the highlands and visit waterfalls. At Aarunya Nature Resort, overlooking the Knuckles Mountain Range, spice gardens, biodynamic agriculture and Ayurvedic-inspired wellness offer another way to connect with the landscape. The journeys can combine two or all three properties, with private transfers available to connect the distinct regions. Across the collection, the philosophy is less about filling every hour and more about allowing Sri Lanka to unfold through meaningful encounters, restorative experiences and the freedom to leave room for the unexpected.

The Curated Take

The most interesting part of this approach is its recognition that a meaningful journey does not need to be measured by how much ground it covers. Sri Lanka offers extraordinary contrasts between coastline, highlands, tea estates and mountain landscapes, and experiencing those transitions at an unhurried pace can be as rewarding as the destinations themselves. Aahaasa’s emphasis on local traditions, working landscapes, wellness and community connections also gives the idea of slow luxury a deeper sense of place. Sometimes the most memorable part of a journey is not what was planned, but what there was finally time to notice.

item.title: This Undiscovered Wisconsin City Is Becoming a Surprisingly Sophisticated Weekend Escape
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Just 90 miles from Chicago, Beloit, Wisconsin, is emerging as an unexpected destination for travelers seeking a weekend getaway with boutique accommodations, ambitious dining, historic architecture and a growing entertainment scene. The launch of Beloit Bound, a new travel-inspiration platform, puts the city’s transformation into focus through curated itineraries, insider recommendations and original destination storytelling. Along the Rock River, this small Wisconsin city offers a collection of distinctive stays, including the MICHELIN Key-recognized Hotel Goodwin, the industrial-chic Ironworks Hotel and the wine barrel suites at Hidden Creek Estates. Its culinary scene features restaurants from the acclaimed Geronimo Hospitality Group, rooftop dining and traditional Wisconsin supper clubs, while entertainment ranges from professional baseball at ABC Supply Stadium to duckpin bowling, golf and gaming. Design enthusiasts can also explore the historic College Park neighborhood and Grand Avenue, where restored homes and architectural character tell another part of Beloit’s story. With major investment reshaping the city, including the development of Ho-Chunk Gaming Beloit, the destination offers a fresh perspective on Midwest travel and an appealing alternative to more familiar weekend escapes.

The Curated Take

Some of the most interesting destinations are the ones travelers haven’t quite put on their radar yet. Beloit’s appeal is its unexpected combination of historic preservation, contemporary hospitality, independent businesses and a developing culinary and entertainment scene. Rather than relying on a single attraction, the city is building an experience around discovery, with boutique hotels, distinctive architecture and places to linger over a memorable meal. For travelers who enjoy finding the next interesting place before everyone else does, Beloit makes a compelling case for a Midwest weekend getaway.

item.title: New York Celebrates Women Shaping the Culinary World
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
For five decades, Les Dames d’Escoffier New York has championed the women shaping the worlds of food, wine and hospitality through education, mentorship and philanthropy. The founding and largest chapter of Les Dames d’Escoffier International marks its 50th anniversary in 2026 with a gala on November 9 at The Lighthouse at Pier Sixty in New York City, honoring celebrated chef, restaurateur and television personality Lidia Bastianich. The evening brings together an impressive collection of culinary talent, including Daniel Boulud, Eric Ripert, Marcus Samuelsson and Jacques Torres, alongside a series of mentor-and-mentee pairings that spotlight the importance of supporting the next generation of women in the industry. Since its founding in 1976, the organization has awarded more than 1,000 scholarships and distributed over $2 million in educational support, while building a professional community spanning chefs, restaurateurs, sommeliers, farmers, writers, educators and hospitality leaders. The anniversary celebrates not only its history, but also the women whose expertise and leadership continue to influence the culinary landscape.

The Curated Take

Food travel is often framed around celebrated chefs, acclaimed restaurants and memorable dining experiences, but the people shaping those experiences deserve recognition, too. Les Dames d’Escoffier New York offers a glimpse into the broader community of women whose work influences culinary culture, hospitality, wine, education and the future of food. Its 50-year milestone is particularly meaningful because it celebrates both achievement and the importance of opening doors for those who follow. In a field where mentorship and the exchange of knowledge help preserve traditions while encouraging innovation, that legacy reaches well beyond the kitchen.

item.title: Four International Awards Put Vietnam’s Ha Long Bay Luxury Cruises on the World Stage
item.dc:creator: Sandra Thomas-Comenole
item.content:encoded:
Grand Pioneers Halong Bay Cruise has earned four international titles in 2026, reinforcing Vietnam’s growing presence in the luxury cruise market and bringing renewed attention to the extraordinary seascape of Ha Long Bay. The Vietnamese cruise brand received World’s Best Green Cruise Line and Asia’s Best Cruise Line at the World Cruise Awards, alongside Best Bespoke Yacht Cruise in Asia and Best Cruise Liner in Asia at the World Luxury Travel Awards. The recognition marks the third consecutive year Grand Pioneers has been honored by the World Cruise Awards, following its wins in 2024 and 2025. Launched in late 2023, the cruise combines spacious accommodations with private balconies, dining, wellness facilities, a Sea Spa and a four-season saltwater pool. Its environmental initiatives include seawater-cooled air conditioning, low-emission engines and advanced wastewater treatment systems, reflecting an effort to balance luxury hospitality with greater environmental responsibility. Developed by Viet Thuan Group, the fleet also represents a distinctly Vietnamese approach to cruise tourism, with the country’s maritime heritage and natural landscapes at the center of the experience.

The Curated Take

Ha Long Bay’s dramatic limestone formations and emerald waters have long made it one of Southeast Asia’s most recognizable natural landscapes. Experiencing the bay aboard an overnight luxury cruise offers a different perspective, allowing travelers to remain immersed in the scenery as the light changes and the day unfolds. Grand Pioneers’ four international awards are notable not only for the recognition of its onboard experience, but also for the attention they bring to Vietnam’s evolving luxury hospitality sector. Its emphasis on environmental technology is particularly relevant in a destination where preserving the natural setting is essential to the future of tourism.
